draft.title: Index laws with variables
card: An index tells you how many times a base is multiplied by itself. In x⁵, the base is x and the index is 5.
Multiply
when you multiply powers with the same base, add the indices. x⁵ × x³ = x⁸. Numbers in front are multiplied: 3x² × 4x⁵ = 12x⁷.
Divide
when you divide powers with the same base, subtract the indices. x⁶ ÷ x² = x⁴. Numbers in front are divided: 12x⁷ ÷ 4x² = 3x⁵.
Power of a power
multiply the indices. (x²)³ = x⁶. A number in front is also raised to the power: (2x²)³ = 8x⁶.
draft.remember: Multiply powers: add indices. Divide: subtract. Power of a power: multiply. Numbers in front follow normal rules.

a.q: What is x⁷ × x² in simplest form?
a.why: Multiplying powers with the same base means adding the indices: 7 + 2 = 9. Multiplying the indices to get x¹⁴ is the rule for a power of a power, not for a product.
a.clue: The bases are the same, so combine the indices by adding or subtracting.

b.why: First (2x³)² = 4x⁶, because both the 2 and the index are squared. Then 4x⁶ × 3x² = 12x⁸, multiplying the numbers and adding the indices. Forgetting to square the 2 gives 6x⁸.
b.clue: Square everything inside the bracket first, including the number.

problems.detail: "An index tells you how many times a base is multiplied by itself" is imprecise. x⁵ is x × x × x × x × x, five factors of x, which is x multiplied by itself four times. Better: "how many times the base is used as a factor" or "how many copies of the base are multiplied together".

check.summary: Both answers check out: x⁹ for (a) and 12x⁸ for (b), and the explanations are correct. The one issue is the card's opening line, "multiplied by itself", which could confuse students about what the index counts and should say "used as a factor" instead.

final.title: Index laws with variables
card: An index tells you how many copies of the base are multiplied together. In \(x^{5} = x \times x \times x \times x \times x\), the base is \(x\) and the index is 5.
Multiply
when you multiply powers with the same base, add the indices. \(x^{5} \times x^{3} = x^{8}\). Numbers in front are multiplied: \(3x^{2} \times 4x^{5} = 12x^{7}\).
Divide
when you divide powers with the same base, subtract the indices. \(x^{6} \div x^{2} = x^{4}\). Numbers in front are divided: \(12x^{7} \div 4x^{2} = 3x^{5}\).
Power of a power
multiply the indices. \((x^{2})^{3} = x^{6}\). A number in front is also raised to the power: \((2x^{2})^{3} = 8x^{6}\).
final.remember: Multiply powers: add indices. Divide: subtract. Power of a power: multiply. Numbers in front follow normal rules.

a.q: What is \(x^{7} \times x^{2}\) in simplest form?
a.why: Multiplying powers with the same base means adding the indices: \(7 + 2 = 9\). Multiplying the indices to get \(x^{14}\) is the rule for a power of a power, not for a product.
a.clue: The bases are the same, so combine the indices by adding or subtracting.

b.why: First \((2x^{3})^{2} = 4x^{6}\), because both the 2 and the index are squared. Then \(4x^{6} \times 3x^{2} = 12x^{8}\), multiplying the numbers and adding the indices. Forgetting to square the 2 gives \(6x^{8}\).
b.clue: Square everything inside the bracket first, including the number.
